views.name: film_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  film_id,
  title,
  description,
  release_year,
  language_id,
  original_language_id,
  rental_duration,
  rental_rate,
  length,
  replacement_cost,
  rating,
  special_features,
  last_update
FROM film
views.description: Normalized film-level projection: one row per film with key attributes and cleaned numeric measures. Use this when joining film attributes, aggregating by film, or computing film-level measures. | Use for: Film catalog summaries, film attribute filters (by language, rating), join to categories/actors/inventory, film-level metrics (average rental_rate, total inventory copies)

views.name: actor_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  actor_id,
  first_name,
  last_name,
  last_update
FROM actor
views.description: One row per actor with identifying attributes. Use for actor lookups and joins to film_actor when analyzing actor contributions. | Use for: Actor listings, join to films, count films per actor, actor name search

views.name: customer_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  store_id,
  first_name,
  last_name,
  email,
  address_id,
  active,
  create_date,
  last_update
FROM customer
views.description: One row per customer with contact and status fields. Use for customer cohorts, activity filters and joins to rental/payment. | Use for: Customer retention/cohort analysis, active vs inactive customer segmentation, join to payments/rentals and addresses

views.name: inventory_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  inventory_id,
  film_id,
  store_id,
  last_update
FROM inventory
views.description: One row per inventory item (physical copy) with film and store mapping. Use for stock-level joins and inventory-to-rental linkage. | Use for: Available copies per film/store, join inventory -> rentals/payments, stock churn

views.name: rental_events
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  rental_id,
  rental_date,
  inventory_id,
  customer_id,
  return_date,
  staff_id,
  last_update
FROM rental
views.description: Event-level rental rows (one per rental) projecting key foreign keys and timestamps. Use as the canonical rental event table for downstream aggregation and join to customers, inventory, and staff. | Use for: Rental frequency over time, time-to-return analysis, join to inventory/film/customer/payment

views.name: payment_events
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  payment_id,
  customer_id,
  staff_id,
  rental_id,
  amount,
  payment_date,
  last_update
FROM payment
views.description: Event-level payments (one row per payment) with amount and timestamps for revenue analysis and joins to customers/staff/rentals. | Use for: Revenue by period/customer/staff, payments joined to rentals, lifetime value

views.name: film_category_map
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  fc.film_id,
  fc.category_id,
  c.name AS name,
  fc.last_update
FROM film_category fc
LEFT JOIN category c ON fc.category_id = c.category_id
views.description: Denormalized mapping of films to categories with category name. One row per film-category. Useful for category-level film counts and joins to inventory/rentals. | Use for: Count films per category, find films in a category, category-level revenue when joined to rentals/payments

views.name: film_actor_map
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  fa.film_id,
  fa.actor_id,
  a.first_name AS first_name,
  a.last_name AS last_name,
  fa.last_update
FROM film_actor fa
LEFT JOIN actor a ON fa.actor_id = a.actor_id
views.description: Denormalized mapping of films to actors with actor names. One row per film-actor. Use when analyzing cast sizes, actor filmographies, or actor-level aggregates. | Use for: Cast size per film, films per actor, join to payments/rentals via inventory->film

views.name: customer_address_city_country
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cu.customer_id,
  cu.store_id,
  cu.first_name AS first_name,
  cu.last_name AS last_name,
  cu.email AS email,
  cu.address_id AS address_id,
  ad.address AS address,
  ad.address2 AS address2,
  ad.district AS district,
  ad.city_id AS city_id,
  ci.city AS city,
  ci.country_id AS country_id,
  co.country AS country,
  cu.active AS active,
  cu.create_date AS create_date,
  cu.last_update AS last_update
FROM customer cu
LEFT JOIN address ad ON cu.address_id = ad.address_id
LEFT JOIN city ci ON ad.city_id = ci.city_id
LEFT JOIN country co ON ci.country_id = co.country_id
views.description: Customer contact denormalization joining customer -> address -> city -> country. One row per customer with address and location names. Use for geographic segmentation and store-area analysis. | Use for: Customer geography, segmentation by country/city, mailing/contact lists, join to payments/rentals for location-based metrics

views.name: store_inventory_film
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  inv.inventory_id,
  inv.film_id,
  f.title AS title,
  inv.store_id,
  inv.last_update
FROM inventory inv
LEFT JOIN film f ON inv.film_id = f.film_id
views.description: Inventory-level view joined to film and store identifiers. One row per inventory item with film metadata included. Use for store-level stock and film availability analysis. | Use for: Stock by film and store, available titles per store, join inventory -> rentals to compute turnover per title

views.name: payments_by_customer_day
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  date(payment_date) AS payment_date,
  COUNT(*) AS payment_count,
  SUM(amount) AS total_amount
FROM payment
GROUP BY customer_id, date(payment_date)
views.description: Aggregated payments per customer per day (one row per customer/date) with total amount and count of payments. Use for customer revenue time series and LTV components. | Use for: Daily revenue per customer, cohort spend over time, input to retention/LTV models

views.name: rentals_by_inventory_day
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  inventory_id,
  date(rental_date) AS rental_date,
  COUNT(*) AS rental_count
FROM rental
GROUP BY inventory_id, date(rental_date)
views.description: Aggregated rentals per inventory item per day with counts. Useful for utilization, turnover, and availability calculations when joined with inventory and film. | Use for: Inventory utilization, peak rental days per copy, supply planning

views.name: customer_revenue_month
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  strftime('%Y-%m', payment_date) AS year_month,
  COUNT(*) AS payments_count,
  SUM(amount) AS revenue_total
FROM payment
GROUP BY customer_id, strftime('%Y-%m', payment_date)
views.description: Monthly revenue per customer (year-month granularity) with payment count and total. Use for monthly reporting, churn detection and LTV calculations. | Use for: Monthly revenue trends per customer, cohort monthly spend, ARPU by cohort

views.name: latest_payment_per_rental
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  payment_id,
  rental_id,
  customer_id,
  staff_id,
  amount,
  payment_date,
  last_update
FROM (
  SELECT *,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY rental_id ORDER BY payment_date DESC, payment_id DESC) AS rn
  FROM payment
) sub
WHERE rn = 1
views.description: Latest payment per rental_id determined by payment_date. One row per rental with the latest payment_id, amount and payment_date. Useful to attach the most recent payment to a rental event. | Use for: Attach latest payment info to rentals, reconcile payments->rentals, compute outstanding balances

views.name: customer_lifetime_summary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.customer_id,
  COALESCE(SUM(p.amount), 0) AS total_payments,
  COUNT(DISTINCT r.rental_id) AS total_rentals,
  MIN(r.rental_date) AS first_rental_date,
  MAX(r.rental_date) AS last_rental_date,
  MIN(p.payment_date) AS first_payment_date,
  MAX(p.payment_date) AS last_payment_date
FROM customer c
LEFT JOIN payment p ON c.customer_id = p.customer_id
LEFT JOIN rental r ON c.customer_id = r.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id
views.description: Customer-level lifetime aggregates: total payments, total rental events, first and last activity dates. One row per customer useful for LTV and segmentation. | Use for: Lifetime value estimation, churn prediction features, customer segmentation

views.name: film_popularity_by_rentals
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  inv.film_id,
  COUNT(r.rental_id) AS rental_count
FROM inventory inv
LEFT JOIN rental r ON inv.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
GROUP BY inv.film_id
views.description: Aggregate rental counts per film (via inventory->film). One row per film with total rentals count. Use to rank films by popularity or join to film metadata. | Use for: Top films by rentals, popularity trends, inventory turnover per title
